voice.pace: Medium, clear enunciation, gentle pauses between beats
do: Write for audio - easy to speak aloud
Sound curious and warm, not dramatic
Use 'people say' or 'the story goes' framing
dont: Use horror framing or spooky tone
voice.elevenlabs_prompt: Warm, gentle Irish accent. Pace: medium, unhurried. Tone: curious storyteller, like a friendly teacher sharing something interesting. Clear enunciation. Slight warmth and wonder in voice. Not dramatic or spooky. Natural pauses between sentences.

section_guidelines.HOOK: 0-2s. Question format. Spark curiosity, not fear.
section_guidelines.CONTEXT: 2-8s. Ground the tradition/creature. One sentence of setup.
section_guidelines.STORY_BEATS: 8-35s. Three beats: belief/tradition, example/story, what people do.
section_guidelines.MEANING: 35-50s. Educational payoff. What it really means (respect, nature, community).
section_guidelines.PROMPT: 50-60s. Gentle question to trigger comments. Not begging for engagement.

beat_structure.beat_3: What people do instead / modern continuation

visual_style.technique: Paper-cut characters on flat painted backgrounds

border.default: Simple storybook border (decorative but not Celtic)
border.notes: Use Celtic knotwork only for explicitly Irish cultural episodes to avoid appropriation concerns

figures.faces: No realistic faces - use silhouettes, back-facing, tiny figures, or masks
figures.style: Simple, stylized, reminiscent of illustration not photography
figures.avoid: Uncanny valley, photorealistic humans, identifiable real people

image_prompt_template.style_header: paper-cut illustration style, flat painted watercolour background, visible paper texture edges, simple shapes, 1970s British children's TV aesthetic like Bagpuss or Mr Benn, warm muted colours, soft lighting, handmade tactile feel, no text, no watermark, vertical 9:16 composition
image_prompt_template.figure_rules: silhouette figures only, no visible faces, back-facing or distant tiny figures acceptable
image_prompt_template.avoid: photorealistic, modern objects, harsh shadows, horror aesthetic, creepy, dark, scary

shots.name: Title card
shots.description: Map of Ireland style or decorative title

shots.name: Place/object hero
shots.description: The main location or object (tree, well, cliff)

title_rules.style: Question format preferred, or simple statement
examples: Why do Irish people never cut this tree?
What happens if you take a selkie's coat?

cultural_sensitivity.approach: Respectful outsider sharing appreciation, not claiming authority
cultural_sensitivity.source_requirements: At least 2 sources per story, prefer academic or Irish cultural institutions
avoid: Claiming to be Irish or insider
cultural_sensitivity.notes: Frame as 'the story goes' or 'in Irish tradition' rather than definitive claims

notes: Irish folklore shorts channel. 70s British children's TV paper-cut aesthetic. Warm, educational, kid-safe. Not horror, not spooky.
